sources.entry: lancedb - A developer-friendly embedded retrieval database for multimodal AI.

summary.one_liner: LanceDB is an open-source embedded retrieval database for multimodal AI that stores and searches vectors, metadata, and multimodal data built on the Lance columnar format.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LanceDB as a database for vector search, built on the Lance columnar format, intended to store, index, and search multimodal data and vectors. It lists vector similarity search, full-text search, and SQL as supported query methods. It states that it can store and filter vectors, metadata, and multimodal data such as text, images, videos, and point clouds. Advanced features named include zero-copy access, automatic data versioning, and GPU support when building vector indexes. The embedded open-source edition runs inside the application process with data on local disk or object storage. A separate commercial LanceDB Enterprise product is mentioned for distributed, production-scale use.
use_cases: multimodal search over text, images, and video
storing and querying AI training or analysis data
embedded retrieval inside a Python or Node.js app
full-text and SQL filtering alongside vector search
keeping versioned datasets without extra infrastructure
how_to_run: Follow the Quickstart doc to set up LanceDB locally (link not included in README text)
notable: Embedded mode runs in-process with no separate server, storing data on local disk or object storage
Combines vector search, full-text search, and SQL in one database
Automatic data versioning without extra infrastructure
Zero-copy access on the Lance columnar format
GPU support for building vector indexes
caveats: The README's install section gives no concrete commands; it only points to a Quickstart doc
The README does not state a license
Distributed production-scale search is offered only in the LanceDB Enterprise product
keywords: search images and video by similarity
